title: Ashaveri Retention Manifest (v2)
description: The layout of a retention manifest: the one artifact that states what a deployment kept, what it retired, how long it has actually held what remains, and, from this version, which material of the appraisal context it held at the instant it stamped. Unlike the receipt and the pack, this document is not signed. It is a JSON file a deployment writes about its own store, and a reader verifies it by recomputation against the chain the pack publishes rather than by a signature over it, which is why every member below has exactly one source and none of them is a second opinion about something the store already knows. Its trust arrives from outside it: the epoch inventory names this file's location and carries sha256 over its bytes in `packs[].retentionSha256`, inside that inventory's own signature, so the bytes of a manifest are evidence for a reader that holds the inventory sealing them and are the deployment's say-so for a reader that holds only the file. `packages/receipt/src/retention.ts` reads this layout and writes it, and the epoch inventory's fold refuses a presence observation arriving under a digest no entry of the run states, which is what keeps a manifest handed on its own from being read as evidence. The map is closed, as the receipt and pack twins close their signed maps: a member `v: 2` does not define is a malformed manifest, not a member a reader agreed to forget, and the same holds of every block below it. This version adds one member, `presence`, and nothing else: `v`, `at`, `policy`, `retained`, `retired`, `chain` and `duty` are version one's members, unchanged in name, order, width and meaning, and a version one document naming no `presence` stays whole under its own layout rather than being read as a manifest that held nothing. On the two chain endpoints: `chain` repeats the anchor and the head here, in this artifact's own words, rather than deferring to the pack that may carry the same store's state. That is what the shipped writer does, it is what the bytes say, and it is the honest reading for a document that travels alone, because the published pack manifest (`packages/receipt/pack.cddl`) names seven members and none of them is this manifest or a digest of it, so a reader holding a pack has nothing to inherit these two values from. Where both artifacts describe one store at one instant the two pairs have to agree, and that agreement is a reader's check rather than a keyword: a pack's endpoints are inside a signature and this manifest's are not, so a pair here that disagrees with a pack's is evidence about the manifest, not about the chain. On the duty: `duty.met` is the arithmetic the writer performed on the two integers beside it, `heldSeconds >= requiredSeconds`, and it is not a conclusion about a legal duty. The pack format leaves its equivalent out on purpose and this artifact states it, which is a difference between the two documents rather than an oversight in one of them. Where the duty is routed to applicable Union financial-services law, the period is the deployment's to state and this estate supplies no default for it, so `requiredSeconds` is a claim about the deployment's reading of that law and nothing here can check it. The same holds of the one article that names a period at all. Article 19(1) asks for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, of at least six months, and yields to applicable Union or national law in particular in Union law on the protection of personal data, which can move what a deployment owes in either direction. A layout that refused a shorter period would be second-guessing a lawful reading with a number this estate owns, so this layout enforces no period for any of the three labels. What this repository does state is a configuration fact rather than a legal reading, the default age bound `gateway/src/store.ts` publishes, and section 5.3 of this specification is where that number is given.

v.description: Format version. Exactly one version is defined by this file, so this is a constant rather than a discriminant and a document naming another version is not this one. A reader refuses a version it does not know.

at.description: Unix seconds, the instant generation began. Stamped before the store is read rather than after it, so a slow store cannot make the manifest claim a later time than the window it describes; `duty.heldSeconds` is measured against this instant and nothing else, and `presence` states what was held at it.

policy.description: The retention configuration the deployment was opened with, as an intention rather than a fact: the bounds it asked the store to enforce. Absent means no such bound configured, which is not the same document as a bound of zero. The store's own clock is deliberately not here, because one clock governs the retirement and a manifest stamped from a second one would report a window the configuration that produced it cannot reproduce.

retained.description: What the store holds right now, reported by the store itself and copied verbatim: the earliest and latest stamps surviving and how many records they cover. This is the survivor set, so it says nothing about why anything is missing from it, which is what `retired` is for.

retired.description: What left, in total and event by event, and under which bound it left. The only place the deployment says which bound removed what.

chain.description: The two endpoints a reader walks between, stated here as the store reports them. This artifact carries no signature, so a pair read here is the deployment's own report about its own store, and where the same store is also packed the authoritative pair is the one inside the pack's signature: two pairs that disagree are a finding about this document, not about the chain. See the header for why the block is repeated rather than deferred.

duty.description: The article the manifest is written against, the period it takes that article to require, the time actually held, and the comparison of the last two.

presence.description: What the store held of the appraisal context at `at`: the collateral and validity documents it had, how many of each, each named by the digest of its own bytes and each stated under the root or chain value it was believed under. It is a statement about one instant and about the past, and it stays true whatever happens to those bytes afterwards, which is why it is what this artifact can carry at all: nothing here states that the material is reachable now, that it will be when a reader arrives, or that it is anywhere a reader can fetch. Reach is assembled from these observations folded across a run by the epoch inventory, `packages/receipt/epoch-inventory.cddl` and its reader, which is the source of the half this document does not carry, and this block is the source of the half that fold cannot state for itself: what one store held at one sealing instant. A manifest that held nothing of a family states an empty list beside a count of zero; it does not leave the family out.

maxAgeSeconds.description: A receipt is served while its issuance stamp is at or after `at` less this many seconds. Absent means no age bound configured; zero is a bound that keeps effectively nothing, and a reader has to tell the two apart.

maxCount.description: How many receipts are served. Absent means no count bound configured. This bound closes a long window sooner than the age bound does, which is why both travel with every trim.

policyState.description: A retention policy as the artifact states it: an absent bound means no cap rather than zero. The same pair of members appears at the top level, where it is what the deployment configured, and inside each trim, where it is what was in force at that compaction.

from.description: Unix seconds, inclusive: the oldest issuance stamp still held. Zero with a `count` of zero is an empty store reporting the zero window, and `at` less that zero is not a measurement of how long anything has been held.

to.description: Unix seconds, inclusive: the newest issuance stamp still held. Both edges of a window the store served, which is not the half-open interval a pack answers for.

count.description: How many receipts are held between the two stamps. The member that decides whether `from` means anything, and the one a reader compares against the totals in `retired`.

window.description: The surviving set, bounded by the stamps actually on the volume rather than by the bounds configured.

byAge.description: Receipts retired because they fell past the age bound, including those dropped before any compaction wrote them down.

byCount.description: Receipts retired because the count bound evicted them, on the same basis.

trims.description: One entry per compaction, in the order the store wrote them, oldest first. An empty array means nothing has been compacted yet, which is a statement about the file rather than about the totals beside it: retirement happens as the store drops records, and a trim is only written when space is reclaimed.

retired.description: The retirement history: two totals by cause and the events behind them. A `window()` report cannot supply any of it, because the survivors carry no record of why their neighbours are gone.

at.description: Unix seconds, the stamp the compaction wrote.

byAge.description: How many receipts that one compaction removed for age.

byCount.description: How many it removed for count.

under.description: The bounds in force at that compaction, read off the trim record's own payload rather than out of memory, so an event survives a later reconfiguration of the store. This is why a long-ago trim can be read without knowing what the deployment was configured to do at the time.

trimEvent.description: One compaction, with the policy that caused it. Each entry corresponds to one trim record at the front of the store's file, whose payload layout and byte offsets section 5.2 publishes; that record stores an unconfigured bound as zero, while this artifact stores it by leaving the member out, so a reader moving between the two media has to convert that one thing and nothing else.

anchor.description: The digest the oldest retained receipt was chained from: thirty-two zero bytes before any retirement, otherwise the seam a trim record carried. Lowercase hex, which is how this estate writes bytes it means a reader to compare.

head.description: The digest of the last receipt in the chain. Stating it is what makes deletion detectable, because a run of receipts the reader was never handed leaves the walk short of this value.

chain.description: Both endpoints, as the store reports them at `at`. Neither is derivable from this artifact, which carries no receipts.

article.description: Which obligation the manifest is written against. The three labels are the closed set the shipped writer's own type admits, which is why they are an enum here; the pack container deliberately leaves its equivalent a plain string because the duty registry is a reader's question rather than that format's, so the two artifacts take opposite stances on one question and a reader should know it. 19(2) and 26(6) route a financial institution's logs into applicable Union financial-services law, where the applicable period is longer and is not this estate's to name.

requiredSeconds.description: Seconds the deployment takes that article to require, at least one so that a stated period is a period. The layout bounds no article's value: the routed articles name no period at all, and the article that does makes its six months a floor beneath a judgment about intended purpose that other Union or national law can move in either direction, which is the deployment's reading rather than a fact a schema here can adjudicate.

heldSeconds.description: Seconds the store has held the oldest receipt it retains, measured at `at`: `at` less `retained.from`, and zero for an empty store rather than a subtraction from the epoch, because a deployment that has never issued a receipt has not held anything for six months, it has held nothing.

met.description: Whether `heldSeconds` is at least `requiredSeconds`, computed by the writer. This is arithmetic over the two integers above it and a reader with a copy of the file can recompute it in one comparison, which is the only reason it may be stated at all: nothing here concludes that a duty was discharged, because whether a per-request receipt is a log the named article requires turns on the system and the actor, and neither is settled by this document.

duty.description: The duty, the period taken from it, the time actually held, and the comparison of the last two. The map is closed and no period is bounded, so a manifest is malformed for a member that is missing, unnamed or of the wrong type, and never for a number this layout would disagree with. Which period an article requires is a legal reading of the deployment's, and the conditional that once enforced the six-month floor of Article 19(1) is deliberately absent, because that article lets applicable Union or national law move the period in either direction and a refusal here would overrule it. What this repository does publish is its own default age bound, `MINIMUM_RETENTION_SECONDS` in `gateway/src/store.ts`, a configuration fact stated in section 5.3 of this specification and pinned against that constant by a test rather than by this sentence.

collateral.description: The vendor-signed material the store held at `at` and appraised evidence against: the certificate chain a quote was presented by, and the documents a platform's own statement is read under. Stated as a count and one entry per document, each named by the digest of the bytes held and each named beside the value it was believed under.

validity.description: The validity material the store held at `at`: the window and the appraisal the same evidence was read in. The same two figures as the collateral family, because the two families are one statement read two ways and a fold that could ask one and not the other would be guessing at which half a store kept.

presence.description: The appraisal context this store held at the instant it stamped, in the two families that context arrives in. Both members are required, and both are held lists rather than optional members, because the two findings a reader is owed apart are that a store held nothing of a family and that a manifest said nothing about it: the first is an empty list beside a count of zero and the second is a malformed document. Nothing here states that any of these bytes is reachable, is still on the volume, or was ever fetched by anybody; the claim is about one instant and it stays true whatever comes after it.

count.description: How many documents of this family the store held at `at`, as the store counted them. `held` is the list beside it, and a reader recomputes one against the other: a count that is not the length of its own list is a malformed manifest rather than a store that held less than it said, which is the same division the duty block draws between arithmetic and a reading of it.

held.description: One entry per document held, in no order that bears anything: a reader matches an entry by the digest it names, the way the inventory matches the rows of its own two folded lists. The list carries no floor because an empty one is the statement that this family was held nothing of at that instant, and a manifest that invented an entry to satisfy a floor would be attesting material the store never had.

presenceFamily.description: One family of the appraisal context: the store's own count, and the documents behind it. Two figures, not one, because the count is what the store reports about its volume and the list is what it reports about each document, and a fold that had only the list would be counting the deployment's enumeration rather than the store's holdings.

sha256.description: sha256 over the bytes of this document as they sat on the volume, lowercase hex. This artifact carries no copy of those bytes, so the digest is the only name it can give them and the only thing a reader with the bytes can compare; a document named twice within one family is a malformed manifest, because a fold that met one digest twice cannot tell whether the store held one document or reported it twice.

under.description: What this document was believed under, as the store held it: a root, or the end of a chain.

presenceHeld.description: One held document and the value it was believed under. Both are required: a digest with no value beside it names material no reader can weigh, and a value with no digest names a belief about nothing.

kind.description: Which of the two ways a document is held to be believed this entry states. `root` is the self-signed end carrying the name the material is read under; `chain` is the sequence of certificates the document was presented by, named at its far end. Two labels and no third, because a store either held the thing that signs or held the run of things that lead to it, and a reader weighing whether it can repeat that weighing needs to know which of the two it is being told about.

value.description: The digest of the bytes this document was held under: the root's own bytes, or the last certificate of the chain as it was stored. Lowercase hex like every other digest here, and stated as a name rather than a copy, because this artifact carries no certificate for anybody.

presenceUnder.description: The root or chain value one held document was believed under, as a label and a digest. Neither figure says the belief was well founded: whether a root signs what it claims to, and whether a chain runs to it, are a reader's own checks with its own pins, and this block states only which value the store kept beside which document.
